mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-over-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last four weeks indicates a sustained recovery trend, which will continue to drive retail and recreation activity higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, indicating a reversal of the observed recovery trend.

mechanism_narrative: As RESIDENTIAL mobility continues its decline, falling below 12.0% from baseline, it signals a critical shift in daily routines where people spend significantly less time at home, directly increasing out-of-home activities including retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 12.0% but RETAIL_REC mobility does not increase in the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous and sustained increases in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility over the past four weeks indicate a broader return to pre-pandemic commuting and work patterns, which will collectively drive increased footfall and spending in retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility continue to increase, but RETAIL_REC mobility declines over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The broad-based increase in mobility across RETAIL_REC, WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and PARKS categories suggests an ongoing and stable 'reopening' policy regime, which will continue to support and encourage further growth in retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: New policy announcements or public health indicators signal a tightening of restrictions, or mobility trends reverse across multiple categories.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-on-week decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility over the past four weeks signifies a sustained shift in public behavior away from home-bound activities, directly translating to increased out-of-home engagement and higher RETAIL_REC mobility over the next week.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases week-on-week, indicating a reversal of the trend towards out-of-home activities.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week increase in PARKS mobility (e.g., greater than 10 points) indicates a surge in outdoor activity and social interaction, which typically spills over into increased foot traffic and spending in nearby retail and recreation establishments over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: PARKS mobility increases by more than 10 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC mobility declines in the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The combined trend of increasing GROCERY_PHARM mobility and decreasing RESIDENTIAL mobility suggests a return to more active and varied daily routines, where essential errands are increasingly combined with discretionary retail and recreation activities, driving RETAIL_REC up over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility increases and RESIDENTIAL mobility decreases, but RETAIL_REC mobility remains flat or declines over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In the current recovery regime from deeply depressed mobility, any continued upward trend in WORKPLACES mobility will disproportionately drive RETAIL_REC as people increasingly combine their return to work with leisure and shopping activities, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility continues to increase, but RETAIL_REC growth decelerates significantly or reverses its upward trend.
